title: Orion Payments — inference characterization and cost/latency sweep (POC)
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the benchmarking sweep we ran for Orion Payments during the initial solutions-eng POC (aim: determine configuration that meets 99th percentile latency SLOs for tokenized invoice classification and entity extraction while minimizing per-token cost). Tests focused on short-chat style prompts (system + user ~120 tokens) and mid-length extraction tasks (input up to 1,200 tokens, output 20–60 tokens).

High-level outcome: with a tuned mix of prefix caching, small batching (max_batch=8), and int8 quantization on rw-realtime-13b we can meet Orion's p95 <= 220ms SLO on H100 Dedicated nodes at ~ $2.8 / 1M tokens (in Dedicated capacity). Hosted API cost projection is higher (~$9–$12 / 1M tokens) but gives faster time-to-rollout. For extreme cost-constrained runs, rw-instruct-7b-int8 on A10x provides acceptable throughput at ~60% lower cost but p95 increases to ~420ms, which may violate realtime constraints for low-latency checks.

Scope and goals:
- Evaluate latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), and estimated unit cost across three candidate model variants: rw-realtime-13b, rw-instruct-7b, and rw-embed-2.7b (for auxiliary similarity checks).
- Test on two deployment modes: Dedicated H100 (8x H100-80GB pool prototype) and Dedicated A10/A100 pools (as representative cheaper hardware).
- Explore batching, KV/prefix cache effects, and int8 quantization tradeoffs.
- Produce recommended config for production POC with runbook snippets to reproduce.

Test harness and environment:
- Test harness: se/orion/bench-runner v0.5 (attached in GH PR). Repro commands: 
  - python bench_run.py --model rw-realtime-13b --instances 4 --batcher max_batch=8 --cache prefix:enabled --quant int8 --mode workers
  - samples driven by a 10k-query corpus sourced from the customer's redacted logs (split 80/20 for warm/cold).
- Network: tests executed from Redwood Dedicated region us-west2 (customer requested us-west latency).
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (client-observed), token throughput, GPU util, mem usage, KV cache hit ratio, and cost estimates using Redwood internal pricing matrix.

Workload profiles used:
1) Fast-check (SC): short prompts used by fraud route (system+user ~40–120 tokens, expected output <=40 tokens). 60% of traffic.
2) Extract (EX): invoice extraction tasks (input 600–1200 tokens, output 20–80 tokens). 30% of traffic.
3) Embedding-check (EMB): similarity check calls (rw-embed-2.7b) invoked for 10% of sessions.

Key configurations swept:
- max_batch_size: [1, 4, 8, 16]
- kv_cache: [off, prefix_cache_enabled (90% hit on repeated forms), full_kv_cache]
- quant: [fp16, int8]
- model variant: [rw-realtime-13b, rw-instruct-7b, rw-embed-2.7b]
- routing policy: [latency-first, cost-first, region-fallback]

Representative results (aggregated):
- rw-realtime-13b (H100 Dedicated, fp16, max_batch=8, prefix cache hit ~78%): p50=34ms, p95=190ms, p99=310ms, throughput ~1,150 tokens/sec per GPU, est cost = $2.8 / 1M tokens. CPU/GPU util: GPU 62% avg. Notes: warm prefix cache critical for SC profile; cold starts on EX incur p95 spikes up to 420ms due to KV cache population.

- rw-realtime-13b (H100 Dedicated, int8, max_batch=8, prefix cache hit ~78%): p50=30ms, p95=170ms, p99=290ms, throughput ~1,420 tokens/sec per GPU, est cost = $2.1 / 1M tokens. Observed minor quality blips on semantic extraction tests (~0.7% drop in entity F1 on a small labeled subset). Recommendation: int8 acceptable for classification/labeling when combined with eval set gating; avoid for money-critical decisioning until production eval pass.

- rw-instruct-7b (A10 pool, int8, max_batch=8): p50=48ms, p95=420ms, p99=780ms, throughput ~520 tokens/sec per GPU, est cost = $1.1 / 1M tokens. Good cost profile but misses p95 SLO for SC profile.

- rw-embed-2.7b (A10x, fp16, no batching): p50=11ms, p95=42ms for a single vector call. Throughput ~2,400 vectors/sec. Cost small relative to gen calls but important contributor for end-to-end latency when called synchronously. Recommendation: run embeddings asynchronously where possible and amortize by batching requests to the embedding endpoint (batch_size=64 gave best throughput/latency tradeoff).

Batching and latency tradeoffs:
- Increasing max_batch from 1->8 improved throughput by ~2.6x for rw-realtime-13b with minimal p95 impact under SC profile; max_batch=16 reduced p95 predictability for EX (longer seqs) and increased tail latency due to fill-wait.
- For Orion's SLO mix (95% SC, 30% EX overlap), recommended max_batch=8 with dynamic batching disabled for the last-microsecond latency path (i.e., route small SC requests to a low-latency pool).

Cache behavior:
- Prefix cache yielded the best wins: with a 78% hit rate we saw p95 reduction ~32% and cost drop ~21% normalized to token counts. Cold-cold runs (no cache warmup) show p95 spikes—practical mitigation is short warmup window at deploy or background prewarm for frequently seen invoice templates.

Quality impact of quantization:
- Quantization to int8 improved throughput and lowered cost as expected. We ran a labeled quality set (n=1,200 extraction pairs). rw-realtime-13b-int8 showed a 0.7 point absolute F1 drop on entity extraction vs fp16 baseline. For classification tasks the drop was negligible (<0.2%). Decision: use int8 for user flows that are non-critical (risk-tolerant) and keep fp16 for high-stakes paths.

Cost modeling (back-of-envelope):
- Dedicated H100 pool (amortized): $2.8 / 1M tokens (rw-realtime-13b-fp16, with prefix cache)
- Dedicated H100-int8: $2.1 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated A10-int8 (rw-instruct-7b): $1.1 / 1M tokens (higher latencies)
- Hosted API (single-region, fully-managed): estimated $9–$12 / 1M tokens (includes margin, multi-az, infra costs)

Operational recommendations (POC->prod):
1) Start POC with Dedicated H100 pool and rw-realtime-13b-int8 + prefix cache enabled. Include an automated canary for extraction tasks on fp16 to compare quality over first 72 hours.
2) Configure routing: latency-first policy routes SC (short) to low-latency H100 pool; cost-first routes non-critical bulk batch jobs to A10 pool.
3) Batching: set max_batch=8; set latency cap of 150ms build-time sampler that bypasses batching for real-time checks (i.e., small queue cut-over).
4) Metrics: instrument per-route token counts, cache hit ratio, model F1 on rolling eval sets, and set regression alerting if F1 drops >0.5 pts or p95 rises >20%.
5) Pre-warm strategy: perform periodic template-driven prewarm jobs following deploys to keep prefix cache warm for top 20 templates.

Repro runbook (short):
- Clone GH PR and ensure bench-runner v0.5 installed.
- Provision playground dedicated pool: se/provision/h100-orion (internal script).
- Run (example): python bench_run.py --corpus orion_corpus_10k.json --model rw-realtime-13b --pool h100-orion --max-batch 8 --cache-prefix true --quant int8 --duration 45m
- Postprocess: python analyze_results.py --out results/orion_h100_int8_max8.json

Open questions and risks:
- Customer requires 99th percentile guarantee for some regulatory checks — our measurements show p99 spikes that need mitigations (we should propose a dedicated hot-pool or synchronous fallback to a smaller model).
- Labeled extraction set size is small (n=1.2k). Recommend full labeling run (5k–10k) to better quantify int8 impact before rolling out on money-movement flows.
- Network variance: tests run from us-west2; customer has multi-region traffic (EU). Need repeat runs in eu-west1 to validate region routing policies.

Next steps (action items):
- (Asha) Expand labeled eval set to 5k examples and re-run quantization quality matrix by 2026-11-10.
- (Marcus) Prototype prewarm job and validate cache hit improvement on a deploy cycle by 2026-11-05.
- (Ivy) Run a eu-west1 replicate sweep for peak-hour window by 2026-11-08 and report differences.
- (Diego) Draft a customer-facing one-pager summarizing cost vs latency options and recommended starting config (target: 2026-11-09).

Appendix: raw sample bench command snippets, interesting logs and quick plots are in the linked GH PR.

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts:
- Consider experimenting with hybrid routing (small requests to rw-instruct-7b-int8 if under confidence threshold, else escalate to rw-realtime-13b).
- If Orion accepts slightly higher p95 during business hours, could shift to A10 pool for non-peak windows to shave costs.
- Add a synthetic steady-state generator to bench-runner to surface queueing-induced tails.

End of note.
